### LOW: Wider mixed\-step prefill ships with acknowledged activation peaks above the measured floors
[docs/architecture/hardware\-support\.md:533](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/c9b97074628a3f17caf4db69419f679c685c7ca9/docs/architecture/hardware-support.md#L533) · ADV-002, T-029

The new text at head lines 528\-536 says a mixed step may now carry up to 4,096 prompt tokens beside decode rows\. That working set is still covered only by the unchanged activation reserve\. The cited 2026\-10\-21 measurements put the KV\-subtracted peak 0\.1 GiB above GPT\-OSS's 3\.5 GiB measured floor, a level the previous geometry already reached\. They put Qwen3\.5\-9B 0\.3 GiB above its previous peak, which was already above the 5\.5 GiB default\. The text defers both floors to a future long\-context re\-measurement with platform admission\. That defers the hardCap invariant \(Σ weights \+ KV \+ activations ≤ hardCap\) for those models\. Trigger: consumers, possibly adversarial, send about eight concurrent \~32k\-token prompts to a busy GPT\-OSS or dense Qwen provider\. The un\-reserved activation peak can then exceed the reserve, pressuring OS memory and risking jetsam/OOM or failed requests\. This is an availability issue, not a confidentiality one\. Fix: keep the previous geometry for these models until their measured floors are raised, coordinated with platform admission\. Alternatively, raise their \`measuredActivationFloorsBytes\` or reserve in the same PR\. The code change \(\`EngineV2Factory\.prefillGeometry\`\) was not supplied, so its actual model scoping is unverified\.
